description: - Implement URL reputation engine in Rust (engine.rs) with heuristic, IANA TLD, and pattern-based filters - Expose plugin via PyO3 as `url_reputation_rust` Python extension - Update Python fallback in plugins/url_reputation/url_reputation.py - Add benchmarks, performance comparison script, and stub typings - Expand unit tests to cover Rust-backed and Python implementations The plugin takes less than 7 microseconds to execute. ## 🔗 Related Issue Closes #2907 --- ## 📝 Summary _What does this PR do and why?_ Implements a Rust-accelerated `url_reputation` plugin using PyO3, replacing the performance-limited Python-only path for URL validation. - **Rust engine** (`plugins_rust/url_reputation/`): heuristic checks (Shannon entropy, IANA TLD validation, Unicode/homoglyph detection), domain whitelist/blocklist, and regex pattern filtering - **PyO3 binding**: exposes `URLReputationPlugin.validate_url_py()` returning a plain Python dict; the Python wrapper imports it at runtime with a graceful fallback - **Python fallback** (`plugins/url_reputation/url_reputation.py`): retained for environments where the Rust extension is unavailable; heuristic and regex features are Rust-only - **Benchmarks**: Criterion bench suite and `compare_performance.py` script for Python vs Rust comparison - **Tests**: expanded unit tests cover both the Rust engine (via `#[cfg(test)]`) and the Python wrapper (with and without Rust available) - **Stub typings** (`url_reputation_rust.pyi`): minimal stub exposing only the Python-facing API --- ## 🏷️ Type of Change - [ ] Bug fix - [X] Feature / Enhancement - [ ] Documentation - [X] Refactor - [ ] Chore (deps, CI, tooling) - [ ] Other (describe below) --- ## 🧪 Verification | Check | Command | Status | |---------------------------|-----------------|--------| | Lint suite | `make lint` | Ok | | Unit tests | `make test` | Ok | | Coverage ≥ 80% | `make coverage` | Ok | --- ## ✅ Checklist - [X] Code formatted (`make black isort pre-commit`) - [X] Tests added/updated for changes - [X] Documentation updated (if applicable) - No secrets or credentials committed [X] > > --- ## 📓 Notes (optional) _Screenshots, design decisions, or additional context._

reviews.author: crivetimihai
reviews.body:
## Review: Approved with fixes applied

Solid implementation of the Rust-accelerated `url_reputation` plugin. The Rust engine is well-structured with proper separation of concerns (engine, filters, types), and the PyO3 integration correctly follows established patterns from `pii_filter` and `secrets_detection`.

### What works well
- **Security-first design**: fail-closed on Rust errors, homograph/IDN detection, Shannon entropy checks, IANA TLD validation
- **Graceful degradation**: Python fallback works when Rust module is unavailable
- **Good test coverage**: 24 Rust unit tests + comprehensive Python integration tests
- **Performance**: compiled regex patterns, IP address detection to skip heuristic checks

### Fixes applied (committed)
1. **Cargo.toml** — added `authors`, `repository`, `description`, `abi3-py311` feature, `[profile.release]` (opt-level 3, LTO, strip), `[profile.bench]`
2. **pyproject.toml** — fixed `name` to `mcpgateway-url-reputation`, `requires-python` to `>=3.11`, added `[tool.maturin]` section
3. **deny.toml** — added cargo-deny license policy config (all other Rust plugins have this)
4. **`.gitignore`** — removed plugin-level .gitignore (parent `plugins_rust/.gitignore` covers it)
5. **Logger calls** — replaced f-string interpolation with lazy `%s` formatting
6. **Tests** — added 8 new tests: Rust error fallback path, Python fallback with HTTP allowed, clean URL happy path, blocked pattern substring, allowed_patterns not honored in Python, config validator edge cases (empty, None, mixed case)

### Notes for follow-up (not blocking)
- `allowed_patterns` is not implemented in Python fallback (documented, tested, Rust-only feature)
- `blocked_patterns` semantics differ: Python uses substring, Rust uses regex. Simple patterns work in both.
- `URL_REPUTATION_BLOCK` violation code could be added to `PLUGIN_VIOLATION_CODE_MAPPING` in a future PR

reviews.author: crivetimihai
reviews.body:
## Follow-up review: additional fixes applied

After cross-checking with a Codex review, three additional issues were found and fixed:

### Fixes applied

1. **Python whitelist subdomain matching bug** — The Python fallback used `host in set` (exact match only), so `sub.example.com` would NOT match a whitelisted `example.com`. The Rust path and the Python blocked_domains check both do subdomain matching. Fixed to align: `host.endswith("." + d)`.

2. **Misleading code comment in engine.rs** — Comment claimed "a separate lowercased copy is used for pattern matching" but no such copy existed. Pattern matching runs against the trimmed original URL (correct per RFC 3986 — paths are case-sensitive). Fixed the comment to accurately describe the behavior.

3. **README inaccuracy** — "Trim and lowercase the input URL" was misleading. Only scheme and host are lowercased (by the URL parser per RFC). Fixed to describe actual behavior.

### Not changed (design decisions)
- Invalid regex patterns silently dropped with warning (fail-open) — deliberate contributor choice, failing the whole plugin would remove all URL protection
- PyO3 result model omits optional fields (`mcp_error_code`, `http_headers`) — Pydantic defaults handle this correctly

All 24 tests pass.
